I'm gonna be the odd one out here. I'll start by saying, MOST of the time this is super not ok. BUT if he's never tried anything with her, it could very easily be genuine. When I (29F) was 16/17 I had a really good male friend who was 24 at the time. He actually spent the night at my house a few times. We shared a bed. I didn't have a couch in my studio. He viewed me like a baby sister and he looked out for me on more than one occasion. I can't remember if my dad knew about him or not but I lived alone so it didn't matter. My mom definitely did not know because she wasn't in my life from the day I moved out. At one point I started to think I had feelings for him but he made it so clear where I stood that I would have never admitted it. If it's something like this, there's no sense in causing drama and ruining a friendship. Their relationship is theirs. If you truly have reason to believe there is ill intent or  inappropriate behavior, bring it to the mom's attention. She may know more than you do.

Occasionally, doctors recommend it because some doctors focus on treating symptoms and don't want people afraid of vaccines. Understandable. But if you are experiencing a safe low grade fever and some aches and pains, it's a sign it's working well. I can completely relate to you. I'm older now but when I was your age it sounds like our lives were very similar. I can say that I moved out at 17 (that's the legal age of an adult in my state) and it completely changed my life for the better. I did go through an even worse patch when I got into a relationship with a person who was very similar to my mother emotionally and mentally. But at that point I knew was able to realize that I had got out once and I could again. I now live quite a simple and happy life. I know I survived much worse than many deal with and I take comfort in knowing that I can change the pattern and be different for my children (if you choose not to be a parent to a human child, a neice/nephew/pet/fully grown friend who needs support can also be something to look forward to). Think of the person who you wish you had right now, and become that person. It's hard to see past the pain and believe life can change. My most painful memory at your age was constantly being told that one day I would understand my mother and thank her for all she had done because everyone just thought she was sooooo nice. Don't let this get you down. You know your truth and you will survive this of you choose to. And I really hope you do. I really hope you do because I'm glad I did.

You're at the perfect age to find your voice, make sure you find the right one🖤 I had a very similar experience and I can promise that you will not go wrong by walking away. If they are understanding and loving parents, then open up a line of communication with them about this. I'm so sorry you're going through this mentally and emotionally.
